answer_text: Zalando changed Zalando Plus in 2024 from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system rewarding engagement (purchases, newsletter subscriptions), with points unlocking four benefit levels; it was tested in Spain, expanded to France and Austria, and will roll out to more markets in 2025 [1][4]. The awards create a separate performance obligation granting a material right to discounts or free goods/services [2]. The year-end accrual is for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities [3].

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (TRY 1.7 billion) in 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million, TRY 1.1 billion) in April 2024, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.

Both operators agreed to the same extension fee of €120 million (excluding VAT), but Vodafone Turkey paid it in advance via a capital injection, while Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira over 2023–2024.
